__As of: 2026-11-01 · OpenEMS version 2026.11.0-SNAPSHOT (development version, branch develop)__

This page compares three widely used systems that work together with OpenEMS: **Home Assistant**, **evcc** and **openWB**. All three are independent projects and not part of OpenEMS. Details are on the pages xref:user/third-party/home-assistant.adoc[Home Assistant], xref:user/third-party/evcc.adoc[evcc] and xref:user/third-party/openwb.adoc[openWB]. The basis in each case is their source code and the OpenEMS source code; none of this has been tried out.

[#sec-openems-sends-values-via-mqtt]
=== OpenEMS sends values via MQTT

Independently of the three systems, OpenEMS has the component **“Controller Api MQTT”**. It sends channel values to an MQTT broker, e.g. the Home Assistant broker. According to its description, changed values are sent immediately and all values additionally every 5 minutes, under topics such as `+edge/edge0/channel/_sum/GridActivePower+`. Topic filters and the persistence priority can be used to limit what is sent; the connection can be encrypted.

The description of the component also mentions subscribing to control topics. Nothing was found for this in the code of the component; according to the code it only **sends** and does not accept any commands.

[#sec-what-to-consider-when-combining]
== What to consider when combining

* **Only one system controls the storage.** If Home Assistant, evcc and a control function in OpenEMS (e.g. xref:user/storage-control/time-of-use-tariffs.adoc[time-of-use tariff]) issue specifications at the same time, the strictest limit applies in each case. The result is then difficult to understand.
* **Only one system controls surplus charging.** evcc, openWB and xref:user/ev-charging-control/surplus-charging.adoc[surplus charging in OpenEMS] see the same surplus. If two of them run on the same wallbox or on different wallboxes without coordination, they work against each other.
* **OpenEMS limits always apply.** Emergency reserve, battery and grid limits, and xref:user/storage-control/section-14a-enwg.adoc[§ 14a] restrict any external specification (see xref:user/systems/fenecon-home-battery.adoc[FENECON Home battery]).
* **Fixed names.** evcc and openWB mainly read `+_sum+`, openWB additionally the fixed `+meter0+` and `+ess0+`. If the naming differs, the values are not correct.
* **Do not expose ports to the internet.** All three use unencrypted connections in the home network; Modbus has no login at all.
* **Load from queries.** Each connection queries regularly. This is not critical at the intervals described here; many additional scripts with short intervals increase the load on the system.
